topics.topic: Whether and how SQLite-controlled database and journal opens must refuse symbolic links without O_NOFOLLOW
questions: How can a post-start symbolic link encountered when sqlite3 opens the database journal be detected and converted to StoreInternalError when sqlite3 cannot be told to refuse the link?
Are the database file and journal exceptions to the requirement that every open use os.O_NOFOLLOW, or must their opens also satisfy that universal requirement?
How can calls after start guarantee refusal of a database or journal symbolic link when sqlite3 performs those opens without O_NOFOLLOW and the walk occurred only before the connection opened?

quotes: the database file and its journal, which sqlite3 opens and cannot be told to refuse a link, are covered by open_store's walk before the connection opens and by the directory's privacy after;
a symbolic link met by any call after start makes that call raise StoreInternalError with nothing written.
judgement.why: SQLite-controlled opens cannot be made to refuse links, while the same requirement promises that every post-start call encountering one raises StoreInternalError.

topics.topic: Whether open_store may create a missing database file or requires an existing database
questions: Must os.lstat accept a missing database path so SQLite can create the database file, or must the database already exist?
Must a missing database path be accepted so the module can create the database, or must os.lstat successfully find an existing non-symbolic-link database before it is opened?
Must a missing database path be treated as safe so the database can be created, or must the database already exist so os.lstat can find it?

quotes: then open the database file inside data_directory as the module's one SQLite connection with synchronous FULL, after os.lstat finds that path no symbolic link;

Every file and directory the module creates inside data_directory — the database file and its journal, the content-addressed area, the spool area, each run's spool directory, every temporary and every published file — MUST be created owned by the process's effective user and granting no permission to group or others, so that the privacy check of the next start passes on the kernel's own files (A18 rule 2).
judgement.divergence: One implementer treats an absent database path as safe and lets SQLite create it, so a fresh private data directory opens successfully; another requires os.lstat to find an existing database and rejects or fails on a fresh directory, which the caller notices.
judgement.why: The text anticipates creation of the database file but does not say how the required pre-open os.lstat handles a path that does not yet exist.
